newsitem.title: USA: du Pont ruled competent to be tried for murder.
newsitem.headline: du Pont ruled competent to be tried for murder.

text.p: Millionaire John du Pont was ruled mentally competent on Monday and will be tried for murder beginning next month in the slaying of Olympic champion wrestler David Schultz.
Delaware County Judge Patricia Jenkins also ruled du Pont, an heir to the DuPont chemicals fortune, will be held without bail pending trial beginning January 21.
Du Pont's attorneys declined to comment on the decision. They had previously said they would pursue an insanity defence in a trial of du Pont.
Said Delaware County Prosecutor Pat Meehan, "We look forward to January 21 and the beginning of this trial. We're prepared to make our case."
Du Pont has been undergoing treatment at Norristown State Hospital since late September, when Jenkins declared him incompetent for trial.
At competency hearings in September du Pont's former lawyers said he claimed to be the Dalai Lama, the crown prince of Russia and the Christ child.

Du Pont's lawyers argued in court last week that he needed at least two more months of treatment, but hospital officials said he had responded well enough to assist in his defence and understand the charges against him.
Jenkins noted du Pont had been able to oversee his business affairs while in treatment.
Du Pont was charged with the January 26 shooting death of Schultz on du Pont's Foxcatcher estate in suburban Philadelphia.

Schultz lived with his family in a house on the estate and worked as a wrestling coach at a training facility established there by du Pont. The shooting was followed by a 48-hour standoff with police before du Pont surrendered.
